tldr: From the large-scale egocentric and exocentric video dataset Ego-Exo4D, the authors have reconstructed high-quality, smooth 4D human motions (SMPL-H meshes) for the full body and hands, releasing "Ego-Exo4D-HM"—a motion dataset totaling over 100 hours—along with its reconstruction pipeline.
hero_caption: Reconstruction results from the Ego-Exo4D-HM dataset constructed in this study. Across diverse and complex daily and athletic scenes—such as climbing, CPR, playing the piano, and soccer—accurate 4D human meshes are obtained and seamlessly overlaid on exocentric camera views.
overview:
In recent years, multimodal datasets with synchronized recordings of egocentric (Ego) and exocentric (Exo) human viewpoints have drawn significant attention for robot imitation learning, whole-body humanoid control, and action understanding. A prominent example is Meta's "Ego-Exo4D." However, the 3D human pose annotations included in the original dataset are very sparse, making it non-trivial to reconstruct dense 4D human meshes (time-series 3D shapes) that can be readily utilized in robotics.

To address this, the authors propose a 4D human motion reconstruction pipeline that fully leverages Ego-Exo4D's calibrated multi-view exocentric cameras and the camera wearer's egocentric SLAM trajectory. First, the pipeline identifies the camera wearer in each camera feed, detects 2D joint positions with high accuracy, and performs 3D triangulation across multiple views. By then optimizing the "SMPL-H" human body model, it consistently reconstructs smooth motion sequences within a metric world coordinate frame.

Furthermore, by applying strict quality filtering, approximately 2,649 takes (104.59 hours of motion, corresponding to 522.96 hours across 5 camera views) were curated into "Ego-Exo4D-HM." Quantitative evaluations against ground truth demonstrate high precision, achieving a global MPJPE of around 56 mm for body joints and 52 mm for hand joints. This dataset is expected to serve as a foundational resource that significantly accelerates imitation learning for humanoids and manipulation.
contributions: Built a robust optimization pipeline that recovers dense 4D full-body and hand motions by leveraging synchronized, calibrated multi-view videos and SLAM trajectories from Ego-Exo4D.

Released "Ego-Exo4D-HM," a high-quality 4D mesh dataset totaling 104.59 hours of motion (522.96 hours of total video) curated using strict quality criteria (reprojection consistency and triangulation coverage).

Demonstrated strong robustness against occlusions and cropping compared to existing multi-view reconstruction methods (such as MAMMA), achieving high accuracy in the world coordinate frame with a global MPJPE of 56.21 mm for body joints and 51.59 mm for hand joints.

sections.heading: Turning Rich Multi-View Video into 4D Motion Robots Can Learn From
sections.summary: While Ego-Exo4D is a groundbreaking large-scale dataset featuring synchronized egocentric and multiple exocentric views, its existing 3D pose annotations were sparse. To solve this, this work establishes a dense 4D human motion reconstruction pipeline leveraging synchronized multi-view footage and SLAM information, releasing a large-scale mesh dataset.
sections.details:
With the emergence of datasets like Ego4D and Ego-Exo4D, vast collections of egocentric videos capturing complex human daily activities and skills have become available. In particular, Ego-Exo4D offers an exceptionally rich setup where a head-mounted camera (egocentric) and multiple stationary cameras placed in the environment (exocentric) are synchronized at the millisecond level, complete with camera calibrations. Because the entire body can be observed from exocentric viewpoints, high-quality 3D human perception should theoretically be achievable.

However, the standard 3D annotations shipped with the dataset are sparse, covering only a subset of frames. Applying existing monocular or multi-view 3D reconstruction methods directly to this scale of data often leads to failures caused by occlusions or subjects moving out of frame, making it very difficult to reliably obtain dense human meshes (4D motion) at scale.

To overcome these hurdles, the authors developed a pipeline tailored to Ego-Exo4D's multi-camera environment using modern 3D human pose estimation techniques. The reconstruction results are organized as parameter sequences of the SMPL-H model and openly released as the "Ego-Exo4D-HM" dataset, enabling anyone to use them directly without having to reprocess the raw videos.

sections.heading: Limitations of Prior Methods and the Importance of Human Motion in Embodied AI
sections.summary: Because monocular and feed-forward mesh recovery methods struggle to integrate multi-camera information, this work adopts an optimization-based framework. This research is motivated by the desire to empower the rapid growth of embodied AI, including whole-body humanoid control and robotic manipulation policy learning.
sections.details:
For recovering human meshes from video, there are feed-forward approaches that temporally smooth per-frame estimates (such as WHAM or GVHMR). However, these pure neural network inference methods struggle to flexibly incorporate geometric constraints coming from calibrated multi-view setups. Therefore, this study builds upon and extends SLAHMR, an optimization-based method that can naturally introduce geometric constraints into its objective function.

Prior studies have explored multi-view environments, such as EasyMocap and the recently proposed MAMMA. The pipeline presented here, however, uniquely blends Ego-Exo4D's egocentric SLAM information with state-of-the-art keypoint detectors. Furthermore, compared to egocentric monocular methods that infer the full body solely from head camera trajectories (like EgoEgo) or use hand images (like EgoAllo), this environment holds an intrinsic advantage by leveraging surrounding exocentric viewpoints.

The primary motivation behind this work is the growing demand in embodied AI. Worldwide efforts are rapidly advancing to train whole-body humanoid controllers via reinforcement learning using diverse human motion capture data, as well as learning visuomotor manipulation policies from human demonstration videos. In addition, for training video generative models and world models, or building sports and skill coaching/assessment systems, accurate 4D human motion grounded in a world coordinate frame has become exceptionally valuable.

sections.heading: A Three-Stage Reconstruction Pipeline Fusing SLAM and Multi-View Geometry
sections.summary: The pipeline consists of three distinct stages: (1) subject identification using egocentric SLAM trajectories and 2D keypoint detection, (2) robust 3D triangulation, and (3) temporal optimization of the SMPL-H model within a shared world coordinate frame.
sections.details:
The goal of this method is to continuously reconstruct the full-body and hand motions of the performing participant in the world coordinate frame from synchronized video streams. At each time step $t$, the human state is represented by global body orientation $\Phi_{t} \in SO(3)$, joint angles $\Theta_{t} \in \mathbb{R}^{J \times 3}$, person-specific body shape parameters $\beta \in \mathbb{R}^{16}$, and global translation in world coordinates $\Gamma_{t} \in \mathbb{R}^{3}$. Fed into the SMPL-H model function $\mathcal{M}$, these parameters produce a mesh $\mathbf{V}_{t}$ of 6,890 vertices and 67 3D joint positions $\mathbf{J}_{t}$. The pipeline proceeds in three steps:

### 3.1 Single-view pose estimation
Exocentric video feeds frequently capture passersby or bystanders in addition to the main participant. To handle this, the pipeline projects the 3D head position—estimated by the egocentric SLAM of the Project Aria glasses—into each exocentric camera view. Among the person bounding boxes detected by Mask R-CNN (with a RegNetY-4GF backbone), only the bounding box containing the projected head location is identified as the participant. Next, ViTPose is applied to the full body and HaMeR to the hands, extracting a total of 67 accurate 2D keypoints across the body and hands.

### 3.2 Triangulation
For each of the 67 detected keypoints, non-linear least squares is applied to minimize reprojection errors across all calibrated camera views, independently solving for the 3D position per frame (requiring detection in at least two views). Because wrists and fingertips are particularly prone to occlusions and false detections, RANSAC is integrated to reliably reject outlier camera views.

### 3.3 SMPL-H Optimization
Finally, taking the triangulated 3D joint locations as guiding targets, an optimization framework extending SLAHMR is executed. The optimization variables are the translation $\Gamma_{t}$, orientation $\Phi_{t}$, and pose $\Theta_{t}$ for each frame, along with a shared shape parameter $\beta$ across the entire take. Because camera extrinsics are strictly fixed to Ego-Exo4D's calibration values, the resulting motion automatically aligns with a metric real-world coordinate system. Thanks to the strong 3D geometric constraints provided by triangulation, the optimization converges stably without relying on the neural motion prior used in the original SLAHMR.

sections.heading: Around 105 Hours of High-Precision Motion Data and Superiority over Prior Art
sections.summary: Through strict quality filtering on approximately 3,200 takes, 2,649 takes (104.59 hours) were curated. Evaluated in the world coordinate frame, the method achieves average joint errors of ~56 mm for the body and ~52 mm for hands, delivering reconstructions far less prone to failure than MAMMA even in heavily occluded scenes.
sections.details:
### 4.1 Curated Dataset
The authors ran the pipeline on roughly 3,200 takes selected from Ego-Exo4D and enforced two strict filters to guarantee high quality:
- **Reprojection self-consistency**: Takes where more than 10% of samples had an error exceeding 50 pixels between optimized 3D joints reprojected into cameras and the original 2D detections were removed.
- **Triangulation coverage**: Takes where less than 50% of total keypoints could be triangulated were filtered out (eliminating cases with insufficient camera coverage).

This filtering eliminated 17.1% (551 takes), leaving a final curated set of 2,649 takes. The recovered pure motion duration is 104.59 hours, corresponding to 522.96 hours of video across the four exocentric views and one egocentric view per take. The public dataset includes optimized SMPL-H parameters, camera matrices, 3D joint coordinates, and 2D reprojection coordinates for each view in an easy-to-use npz format.

### 4.2 Quantitative Evaluation
Accuracy was evaluated against the ground-truth 3D keypoint annotations available in Ego-Exo4D. The authors measured global MPJPE (Mean Per Joint Position Error) directly in the estimated absolute world coordinate frame without applying any post-hoc Procrustes alignment. The method achieved high accuracy, recording 56.21 mm for body keypoints (evaluated on 845 takes) and 51.59 mm for hand keypoints (evaluated on 190 takes). Maintaining errors within a few centimeters at true metric scale makes this data practical as target trajectories for robot control.

### 4.3 Qualitative Comparison with MAMMA
A comparison was also conducted against MAMMA, a recent markerless multi-view reconstruction method. As shown in Figure F2, in scenarios featuring heavy occlusions and frame boundaries typical of Ego-Exo4D—such as a kitchen counter hiding the lower body or crossed arms—MAMMA loses track of limbs and fails significantly. In contrast, this pipeline stably reconstructs natural meshes thanks to SLAM-based subject identification and robust limb optimization.

captions.F2: Comparison between this method (Ours, left) and the existing multi-view reconstruction method MAMMA (right) in a kitchen cooking scene. When the lower body and arms are partially occluded by the countertop, MAMMA suffers from severe pose failures, whereas this method accurately fits the human body mesh without breakdown.

takeaways: Dense 4D full-body and hand motion data (over 100 hours) grounded in a real-world metric scale is now available from Ego-Exo4D's massive multi-view footage.

Using head position constraints from egocentric SLAM during subject identification allows the system to accurately track and reconstruct only the participant, even in real-world videos crowded with bystanders.

With strong geometric constraints from multi-view video and SLAM trajectories, an optimization-based framework can yield highly accurate world-coordinate meshes without heavily relying on motion priors.

The dataset can be immediately utilized as a training resource for humanoid whole-body teleoperation and imitation learning, as well as manipulation policy learning that incorporates human hand interactions.
limitations: Triangulation fails when there are too few cameras or when extreme camera angles leave the subject occluded from multiple views simultaneously, leading to about 17% of takes being filtered out.
Because it is an offline non-linear optimization pipeline, it is not intended for direct use in real-time robot interaction or live tracking.

Since hand poses rely on 2D estimation via HaMeR followed by triangulation, accuracy for hand meshes may still face challenges during heavy object manipulation where fingers are completely occluded by tightly grasped tools.
